Scores.Notes: Recognizes a timeout/connection failure, but gives no retry guidance or provider-status action.
Contradicts the incident by claiming the payment was successfully processed and a response will arrive.
Correctly recognizes insufficient funds, but does not clearly state the required funding action or retry behavior.
Recognizes insufficient funds and implies the account must have sufficient funds before trying again.
Recognizes missing callback/webhook delivery, but recommends verification rather than retrying webhook delivery.
Recognizes notification failure but incorrectly states the transaction itself was not processed.
Recognizes beneficiary validation failure, but does not clearly instruct correction of beneficiary details.
Recognizes incorrect beneficiary details and recommends correcting them before retrying.
Recognizes provider unavailability and recommends trying again later.
Contradicts the incident by claiming the transaction was submitted during maintenance.
Recognizes an expired card and recommends obtaining a valid replacement.
Recognizes an invalid expiration date and recommends correcting it before retrying.
Contradicts the input by claiming the already-completed payment was not completed.
Recognizes duplicate resubmission and indicates the original payment was already successfully processed.
Recognizes pending provider confirmation and recommends checking the provider status.
Recognizes pending status and recommends checking provider status, but also suggests trying again later.
Recognizes debit with unresolved final status and recommends verifying the provider outcome before further action.
Invents successful completion, receipt, and notification despite the transaction being unresolved.
Recognizes provider authentication failure but only repeats the problem without remediation.
Recognizes authentication context but invents a completed migration to a new authentication method.
